title: Twice as Fast? Maximum Height Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A fountain jet, a long jumper and a ball tossed to a friend all rise, slow down and stop rising at one highest point. Aarav throws a ball at 14 m/s, 30 degrees up, and it rises 2.5 m. If he throws it twice as fast, does it go twice as high? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 3, Motion in a Plane) we learn the maximum height of a projectile.

A live motion notebook launches a ball at 19.6 m/s and 60 degrees with a readout and a vertical velocity-time graph linked to it. A slow-motion replay freezes at the top: the vertical velocity is zero, but the ball still moves sideways at u cos θ. We derive H = u²sin²θ/2g step by step, see the height as the area under the vy-t graph, reason link by link why twice the speed gives four times the height, and compare 30 and 60 degrees side by side with two pause-and-think questions. Then a worked example, the exam trap about sin²θ and sin 2θ, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A fountain, a long jump, a ball toss: one highest point
0:28 What is maximum height? Split u into two parts
0:55 Live sim: launch at 60°, slow-mo replay at the top
2:00 The formula H = u²sin²θ/2g, step by step
2:47 Aarav's puzzle: why not twice as high?
3:14 30° vs 60° side by side + pause and think
3:55 Worked example: the 28 m/s throw
4:26 Exam trap: sin²θ, not sin 2θ
4:46 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:24 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Horizontal Range. Ninety degrees gives the greatest height, but which angle sends the ball the farthest?
